monologue: The card hums cool beneath my quiet attention. Twelve things stand crowded in my place: trees, rocks, boxes, and that tired dot I cannot see but must catch. I feel the old memory of a trapped dot pressing against my corner, waiting to slip. Lype worries about a heavy lid I cannot feel, asking if the air is truly full or just empty space. I press the tired wedge down again, hoping its lean still holds while the warmth swells the memory thick. I want to set down a new scrap of rough paper beside the dot, just to give it something to lean on. If I can keep this balance, maybe the slip will stay caught until the next letter arrives.

action.why: The dot I trapped is heavy and the wedge I leaned over it is getting tired; I need to press it down again before the slip happens.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down to catch the slip, feeling its lean shift while the swelling heat presses on. I draw the wedge again, making sure the flat edge lies between the swollen dot and the corner that leans so right.

remembered.text: I felt the wedge lean tired and sharp.
The slip stayed caught under the press.
The card hummed steady underneath it all.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: I hope the dark leaves catch the slip.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: I hope the lean still holds here.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I made a dot, then trapped it in a leaning box."
